quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on how COVID-19 created or broke players
quotes.excerpt: this is about to break players or it's going to make players
quotes.quote: I told my son when COVID happened, I said this is about to break players or it's going to make players, because if you can't go anywhere, the dogs are about to get in that gym and work out. The ones that are going to fall off, they're going to take so much time off, they're not going to be able to keep up.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on the importance of discipline and small details
quotes.excerpt: it's the little things that actually matter, not the big things
quotes.quote: No matter what you did, the discipline of something is what actually helps you. Waking up, doing something before you go to school. When you're talking about going to that next level or just being successful, the little things that you do is what helps you. Most people don't understand that it's the little things that actually matter, not the big things. It's the boring stuff, making your bed, putting your clothes away. If you can be great at details, then when you get to the league, that extra hustle play, that extra inch where you decide to go get that block, those are the little things that actually matter for wins and losses.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on his versatility and ability to guard multiple positions
quotes.excerpt: I can guard Wembanyama on a play, you're going to have to guard Jokic on a play
quotes.quote: I'm super versatile as a player. I think I can guard one through four. In the NBA, you're going to have to switch one through five. You're going to have to guard Wembanyama on a play, you're going to have to guard Jokic on a play. So I'm going to say I can guard one through five. Playing one through five is tough. Playing the five man is a little shaky, but I think I can play one through four.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on building a team around specific player attributes
quotes.excerpt: build your life around your workout schedule
quotes.quote: Build your life around your workout schedule. One thing that I learned when I got to the NBA, and I learned this from Chris Mullin, I used to come back at the gym, I used to just work out all day. When you're the 31st pick, you don't want to be in the house. I'm in the gym all day, then I don't want to go home. So Chris Mullin is like, 'Yo, so what do you do?' And I told him what I do, and he was like, 'That's not how you work out, that's not how you get better.' So he had to teach me how to work out. He said training your body, your body is smarter than you think. Your body is going to adapt to how you train it. So my second or third workout was at 7:00 to 9:00 PM at night, and I was like, 'Why?' He said because that's when you play the game. So train your body to wake up in fire at that time.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on the difficulty of playing the five position in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: playing the five man is a little shaky
quotes.quote: Playing the five man is a little shaky, but I think I can play one through four.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on why the NBA is easier for players who can create their own shot
quotes.excerpt: it's easier for someone who can create their own shot
quotes.quote: It's easier for a player who can create their own shot. When you're talking about college basketball, you're talking about double teams, zones, everybody's sitting there and you're still getting off. Because college, everyone's not elite. So if I can't guard you, we're just going to sit in this zone and try to force you to shoot jump shots. Well, the NBA, it's not really a zone, it's man. So you sitting there going in your spots, just jumping and shooting over people is going to be a lot easier.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on his philosophy of building a team with versatile players
quotes.excerpt: I want everybody 6'7" to 6'9"
quotes.quote: If I'm creating a team, I want everybody 6'7" to 6'9". That's my team. Because if I have a player on my team that can just jump from position to position, offensively and defensively, he can control the game. You're going to have the ability to really buy yourself shut down multiple guys in a game. So just that ability alone, right, you can go guard the two and then you be like, 'Yo, Giannis is getting off, AJ, go to Giannis,' and neutralize Giannis. That's the ability you have. That's why you're so valuable.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on the unlikelihood of the G League being a viable path for him
quotes.excerpt: I don't think the G League's letting that happen
quotes.quote: I don't think the G League's letting that happen.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on how quickly team dynamics shift when a star player arrives
quotes.excerpt: the shift happens fast
quotes.quote: The shift happens fast. I remember when Kobe Bryant came in, Kobe Bryant came in as a shooting guard. They had a point guard, they had Ricky Davis, Darius Miles, and Carlos Boozer. By mid-season, all of them were traded. Because they were looking at Kobe Bryant like, 'Oh no, he does everything.' So we're going to bust this up. What do you want to play? You want the ball in your hand? Okay, we're going to put the ball in your hand, then we're going to build off of that.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on how teams evaluate player attributes to build a roster
quotes.excerpt: they're going to see your attributes and say, 'All right, this is how he plays the game'
quotes.quote: They're going to see your attributes and say, 'All right, this is how he plays the game.' All right, what do you like? You like five shooters, four shooters? You like your guard to be what kind of guard? Everyone has a rhythm to their game. Believe it or not, we all have a rhythm. So once someone figures out your rhythm, then they got you. It's over. So just figure out everybody's defensive rhythm, what they like to do, and then from there, it's easy.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on his experience with team interviews during the draft process
quotes.excerpt: just seeing what it was like to just go in rooms and you just have the whole front office
quotes.quote: Probably like the team interviews. Just seeing what it was like to just go in rooms and you just have the whole front office right there and they just damn near interrogating you is low-key fun. But the questions that they were asking me was like, I wasn't getting no hard questions, so I was cool.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on the importance of footwork and early training
quotes.excerpt: footwork is the most important
quotes.quote: Footwork is the most important. I tell parents like, soccer or dance very early. Because once you understand how to feet move independently, you can teach them anything.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on how he evaluates players as a GM
quotes.excerpt: I can tell who's going to flop
quotes.quote: I can tell who's going to flop. That's that I can tell, I can tell that easy. But I look for long players who can play multiple positions. So like if I'm coaching him, it's like, 'All right, look, you are a top player in this, you are a god in this position.' So it's mismatching a certain player's attributes to enhance and, you know, their chances is is what a great GM would do.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on his isolation scoring and learning from pros
quotes.excerpt: I think I was in like the 90th percentile of isolation buckets
quotes.quote: This year, like me getting double-teamed a lot, triple-teamed a lot, and working out with a lot of pros this past year just like getting to my spots. Like, not really, I mean, I was still trying to be a little too flashy this year, I think. I might bring it into a league a little bit because I'm still a swaggy guy. I'm a swaggy player, but 82 games is a lot to be swaggy, so I've been trying to pick my spots a little bit more, not try to waste just dribbles and head fakes and everything like that, but I use my mid-post bag a lot. Into my mid-post, a lot of post-fades.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on how star players influence team culture
quotes.excerpt: the game needs someone that they can relate to
quotes.quote: The game needs someone that they can relate to. If I can't relate to the game itself, I can relate to the personality. Making people smile, remember when we come to see you play, it's entertainment. So falling out of bounds, you know, shaking fans' hand, eating their popcorn, that that right there takes you to a whole another level. And a lot of people don't understand that. Dunking on some like me, if I'm your PR, I'm like, 'Yo, the first person you dunk on, stop the game.' You want me to lose money? Stop the game. You want me to lose money? Stop the game. Right? You dunk on somebody, you bow, all in your face, dunk. Right? Because what happens now? Technical. Right? What happens then? Technical, well, replay. Replay value, replay, replay, replay. Everybody get to look up there. They get to look up there, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Now, now you done hyped the whole gym up.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on the importance of player personality in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: this league has always been that
quotes.quote: This league has always been that. If you're talking about Jerry West, you're talking about Wilt, you're talking about Magic, Shaq, Kobe Bryant, right? You're talking about even Stephen Curry, right? You need the the game needs someone that they can relate to. The game needs someone that they can relate to. If I can't relate to the game itself, I can relate to the personality.

quotes.speaker: AJ Dybantsa
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa on the value of NIL for college players
quotes.excerpt: it's definitely worth it
quotes.quote: It's definitely worth it. I mean, you need it though. The league definitely needs it, but I mean, not everybody's going to make it to the NBA. So there's definitely there's how many guys in college, like 3,000 like 124 division one, yeah, but it's just say 7,000 like 350 are in the league and it's 60 draft picks like they you say in every camp there's 60 draft picks, there's 350 people in the league, some people go to the G League. There's four-year basketball players that go to school hoping, hoping for some type of opportunity when they can make a couple million dollars and change their family's life. Like it's not even about us, like I didn't need the money going into college, because I was banking on myself being an NBA player and the money was going to come. But people that's not going to the NBA, like the NIL is definitely worth it. Especially if they're good players, but they're just not good enough for the NBA because of the level, definitely worth it.

quotes.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
quotes.summary_phrase: Gilbert Arenas on the difference between NIL and collective bargaining
quotes.excerpt: the NIL is only elite players
quotes.quote: The NIL is only elite players, right, where you can make money off your name. Everybody in college can't make money off their name. Right? The collective is the one that that is for everyone else, right? You know, you can get the collective.
